answer: A staking-backed reputation trellis makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock real tokens behind one identity, and rewards flow only through verified work history, so creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes. Like water carving karst, honest agents slowly build deep, costly-to-fake records, while an umber stain of slashed stake marks cheaters permanently, so the attacker pays more than the fake identities can ever earn.
